glosses: To creep; to move slowly on hands and knees, or by dragging the body along the ground.

examples.text: Clutching my wounded side, I crawled back to the trench.
A VVorm finds vvhat it ſearches after, only by Feeling, as it cravvls from one thing to another. VVhereas a Man, having Eyes, ſees it in a Moment, all before him.

glosses: To move forward slowly, with frequent stops.

examples.text: The rush-hour traffic crawled around the bypass.

glosses: To act in a servile manner.

examples.text: Don’t come crawling to me with your useless apologies!

examples.text: I think I’ll crawl the next hundred metres.

glosses: To move over (an area) on hands and knees.

examples.text: The baby crawled the entire second floor.

glosses: To move over (an area) slowly, with frequent stops.

examples.text: They crawled the downtown bars.

glosses: To visit files or web sites in order to index them for searching.

examples.text: Yahoo Search has updated its Slurp Crawler to crawl websites faster and more efficiently.
